title: How to Make Him Respect You: 14 Habits That Build Respect
h1: How to Make Him Respect You: 14 Habits Built on Self-Respect
description: How to make him respect you starts with respecting yourself. 14 practical habits around boundaries, honesty and independence, plus when respect is on him.
keyword: how to make him respect you
excerpt: Respect isn't earned by playing games. These 14 habits help you set boundaries, show up as yourself and recognize when the problem is his, not yours.
intro:
Feeling disrespected by someone you care about is painful. Maybe he cancels plans at the last minute, brushes off your opinions, or acts like your time matters less than his. You start wondering what you're doing wrong and how to change it.

Here's the honest truth up front: you can't force anyone to respect you, and if a partner treats you badly, that's on him. What you can do is show up with clear self-respect, communicate honestly and set boundaries, which makes respect far more likely and makes it easier to see when it's missing. This guide on how to make him respect you covers fourteen habits that do exactly that, and the signs that it's time to stop trying.
body:
Why Respect Starts With You

People take cues from how we treat ourselves. When you speak up for your needs, keep your commitments and protect your time, you're quietly teaching others how you expect to be treated. That's not about being demanding. It's about being clear.

Healthy respect in a relationship also runs both ways. The goal isn't to win a power struggle; it's to build a partnership where both people feel valued, listened to and free to be themselves.

Know Your Worth

1. Stop comparing yourself to others

Measuring yourself against his exes, his friends' partners or people online chips away at your confidence. You bring your own mix of strengths, and the right partner values those. If insecurity is a regular struggle, our guide on how to not be insecure can help.

2. Put yourself first sometimes

Being caring doesn't mean always coming second. Keep your own plans, rest when you need it and say no to things that drain you. A partner who respects you will understand.

3. Stay independent

Keep your friendships, hobbies, goals and, as much as possible, your own financial footing. Having a full life of your own means you're in the relationship because you want to be, not because you have nowhere else to turn.

Communicate Clearly and Honestly

4. Say what you mean

Hinting and hoping he'll guess leads to frustration on both sides. Calmly state what you need: "It hurts when plans change last minute. Can you give me more notice?"

5. Don't hide your intelligence or opinions

Share your thoughts, even when they differ from his. Dimming yourself to keep things smooth only teaches him that your perspective is optional. Respectful disagreement is a sign of a healthy relationship.

6. Skip the games and manipulation

Silent treatments, jealousy tests and guilt trips might get a reaction in the moment, but they erode trust. Direct, honest communication earns more respect than any tactic.

Tip: When something matters, say it once, clearly and calmly, at a good time. Repeating it angrily in the middle of an argument is much less likely to be heard.

Set Boundaries and Keep Them

7. Don't do everything he says

Compromise is healthy; constant compliance isn't. If you always go along with his choices about where to eat, who to see and how to spend weekends, your preferences slowly disappear. Speak up for what you want.

8. Teach him how to treat you

When he crosses a line, address it. If he talks down to you, you might say, "I'm happy to talk about this, but not when you speak to me like that." Then follow through by stepping away if it continues. Our guide on how to stand up for yourself goes deeper.

9. Move at your own pace physically

Intimacy should happen when you genuinely want it, not as a way to keep someone interested or to prove anything. Waiting until you feel ready, however long that is, is a form of self-respect, and a partner worth having will respect that choice.

Be Reliable and Own Your Actions

10. Follow through on plans

Respect is a two-way street. Keeping your own promises shows that your word means something and gives you solid ground to ask the same of him.

11. Don't make excuses

When you make a mistake, own it: "You're right, I forgot. I'm sorry." Accountability is a strength, and it makes it easier to expect the same from your partner.

12. Don't be afraid to get things wrong

Trying new things, making decisions and occasionally messing up is part of being a confident adult. You don't need to be perfect to deserve respect.

Be a Partner, Not a Rival

13. Show him respect too

Acknowledge his strengths, listen when he talks and thank him for what he does. Respect tends to grow when both people feel appreciated. If you want to understand what makes many men feel valued, see what men want in a relationship.

14. Challenge him in good ways

Encourage his goals, push back on ideas you disagree with and bring fresh perspectives. Partners who help each other grow tend to admire each other more over time.

Handle Emotions in a Healthy Way

Strong emotions are human, and you're allowed to be upset. What helps is expressing those feelings in a way that leads somewhere: naming what you feel, explaining why and saying what you need. Explosive reactions or tantrums make it easy for the real issue to get lost, while calm honesty is hard to dismiss.

Taking care of your own wellbeing helps here too. Rest, exercise, friends and time alone make it easier to respond rather than react. If you want to build that foundation, read how to be happy with yourself.

What respectful communication sounds like

It helps to have a few phrases ready for the moments when respect is on the line:

  • When he interrupts: "Hang on, I wasn't finished. I'd like to finish my thought."
  • When he dismisses your feelings: "I understand you see it differently, but this matters to me."
  • When he makes a decision for both of you: "I'd like to be part of that decision next time."
  • When a joke goes too far: "I know you meant it as a joke, but that one hurt. Please don't say it again."
  • When you need time: "I'm too upset to talk well right now. Can we come back to this in an hour?"

Notice that none of these involve yelling, insults or threats. They're calm, direct and focused on what you need. Said consistently, they make it clear what you will and won't accept.

Signs respect is growing

Change is often gradual, so look for patterns rather than single moments. He asks your opinion before making plans. He apologizes when he's out of line, without being pushed. He talks about you kindly to friends and family. He keeps his word more often than not. When you set a boundary, he adjusts instead of arguing. These are signs that your relationship is moving in a healthy direction.

When Respect Is His Responsibility

You can do everything on this list and still not be respected. Some people don't change, and some behaviors are never acceptable. Be honest with yourself if he:

  • Regularly insults, mocks or belittles you, in private or in public
  • Controls your money, phone, friendships or where you go
  • Ignores your boundaries after you've clearly stated them
  • Makes you feel afraid, or threatens you in any way

Those aren't signs that you need to try harder. They're signs of an unhealthy, possibly abusive relationship. Our article on mentally abusive relationships explains the patterns to look for.

Tip: If you feel unsafe or controlled, you can talk to someone confidentially at the National Domestic Violence Hotline: call 1-800-799-7233, text START to 88788, or visit thehotline.org.

The Bottom Line

Learning how to make him respect you is really about respecting yourself first: knowing your worth, speaking honestly, setting boundaries and keeping your own life full. Offer him the same respect you expect, and pay attention to how he responds. A good partner will meet you there. If he consistently doesn't, the most self-respecting choice may be to walk away.
takeaways: Respect starts with how you treat yourself and the boundaries you set.
Clear, honest communication earns more respect than games or hints.
Respect is mutual: keep your word and show him respect too.
Ongoing belittling, control or fear are red flags, not problems you can fix by trying harder.

faq.q: How do I get my boyfriend to respect me again?
faq.a: Start with a calm, honest conversation about the specific behavior that feels disrespectful and what you need instead. Then set clear boundaries and follow through when they're crossed. Keep your own commitments and independence. If he responds with effort, things can improve; if he dismisses your concerns repeatedly, take that seriously.

faq.q: What are signs a man doesn't respect you?
faq.a: Common signs include ignoring your opinions, frequently canceling plans, mocking you in front of others, dismissing your feelings, pressuring you to do things you don't want to do, and crossing boundaries after you've stated them. Controlling behavior or anything that makes you feel afraid goes beyond disrespect and is a serious red flag.

faq.q: Can you make someone respect you?
faq.a: Not directly. Respect is a choice the other person makes. What you can do is model self-respect, communicate clearly, set and enforce boundaries, and treat him with respect too. Those steps make respect much more likely and help you see clearly whether he is willing to offer it.

faq.q: Does setting boundaries push men away?
faq.a: Healthy boundaries tend to attract people who are good for you and filter out people who aren't. A partner who respects you will adjust when you explain what you need. If someone pulls away because you have reasonable limits, that usually reveals something important about the relationship rather than a mistake on your part.
